How to read the results

From blocks to behavior

Multi-scale heatmap

Predict a 16-block tile, then predict the precise horizontal block and altitude conditional on that tile. Train against the original block plus 16- and 32-block spatial losses. Several hotspots can emerge in the same distribution.

Adaptation

Every 30 seconds, use the last 32 eligible examples for that player. A training example becomes available after its future endpoint has been recorded. ANIL adapts a small spatial output bias. Meta history learns how much to trust an empirical player heatmap.

Read the ANIL paper

Evidence

The final fit uses eight games. The four latest matches are held out from that fit. Within each held-out match the models adapt online using completed examples. Exact-block comparisons use the same recorded endpoints for every model.

Capture and rendering

The arenas come from captured chunk packets and timed block edits. Tiles show display-quantized horizontal probability, summed over altitude. The benchmark uses full-precision probabilities. Unloaded players and missing frames can leave gaps.
